messages:
marta: quick status — I ran a targeted perf sweep on continuous-batcher+admit controller last night. saw a repeating pattern: when KV hit rate drops from ~18% to ~10% we get admit-rate oscillation and a cascade of soft-429s.
chen: can you paste the high-level numbers? latency impact?
marta: tail latency + p50 both nudge up ~10-15% during oscillation windows, token throughput drops ~22% for ~30-60s stretches. KV miss correlates with smaller batch sizes and more frequent kernel switches.
sam: hmm. sounds like token_budget target isn't compensating for batch shrink. what's current config for the test cluster?
marta: current (canary) config:
```yaml
admit:
  token_budget_target: 120000
  soft_reject_pct: 0.06
  holdback_window_ms: 50
  kv_prefetch_threshold: 0.15
  queue_smoothing: 0.2
```
kai: that token_budget_target is static across models, right? might be too aggressive when kv hits fall and kernel choice flips to slower path.
chen: agree. propose dynamic token_budget that decays proportional to recent kv_hit rolling 5m. e.g. budget *= clamp(kv_hit/0.16, 0.6, 1.0).
marta: I prototyped something like that: when kv_hit < 12% reduce token_budget to 0.75x over 10s ramp. result: oscillation amplitude drops ~40% and soft-429 bursts reduced. downside: slightly lower peak throughput.
sam: can we instead add soft-holdback (micro window) that prefers longer queueing for requests likely to batch (low token requests) and prefer shed for long sequences?
kai: we have request size histograms. cheap to add a lane: small-token-priority. prefer holdback for <=64-token requests. helps batch size without touching global budget.
marta: yeah I ran a micro-experiment: small-token lane + token_budget decay + a small admit jitter. patch diff below (pseudo):
```diff
+admit.lanes.small_token: holdback_ms: 30; priority: high
+admit.token_budget.decay_on_kv_miss: {threshold: 0.12, ramp_ms: 10000, factor: 0.75}
+admit.jitter_ms: 3..20
```
chen: logs from the run show cleaner kernel stability but a small regression in median latency for large sequences (+5ms). acceptable?
sam: tradeoff seems fine if we avoid repeated 429s. can we make large-seq requests fallback to slower but guaranteed kernel path (no soft-429)?
kai: yes we can mark long-seq requests as "priority-fallback" and route to dedicated kernels or slower path with higher token cost but no soft-reject. need to measure cost delta.
admit-bot: deploy status — canary build with small-token-lane + budget-decay deployed to rack-canary-3, started at 2026-03-18T02:00Z.
marta: next steps I propose: 1) run 24h canary with budget_decay + small-token-lane + jitter 2) measure kv_hit buckets (<10%,10-16%,>16%) and per-batch kernel-switch rate 3) add telemetry for "admit_decision_reason" tag on traces.
chen: add a short-run ablation where we: a) disable jitter b) disable holdback lane c) static budget to isolate contributions.
sam: I'll own the ablation runs and dashboard panels. will also add synthetic kv miss flood to stress test.
kai: I'll instrument kernel selection logs to expose chosen kernel id + latency estimate.
marta: cool. if we see stable metrics after 24h we can promote to default with small ramp. if not, rollback and iterate.
chen: noted. can someone create the runbook for rollback thresholds? suggested: soft-429 rate >3x baseline or p95 latency +20% for 30m -> rollback.
sam: creating runbook now and wiring alerts to #eng-runtime-monitoring.
marta: thanks. tagging folks: @chen @sam @kai — please update by EOD UTC. :thumbsup:
